headline: Axelrod 1986 Norms/Metanorms (agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; metanorm seed-mean V=5.942 vs no-metanorm V=2.877; metanorm B=0.139 vs no-metanorm B=0.880

verdicts.gate: P1 plain norm collapses: majority of no-metanorm seeds end with mean vengefulness < 2.5 (norm not enforced)
reasons: only 6/20 no-metanorm seeds ended below V<2.5 (need >= 11 for a majority); no-metanorm seed-mean final V = 2.877 (range [0.045, 5.165], std 1.397) — the plain norm does not collapse in a majority of seeds here

verdicts.gate: P2 metanorms raise enforcement: with-metanorm seed-mean final vengefulness > no-metanorm seed-mean final vengefulness
P3 contrast holds: vengefulness rises (V_meta - V_nometa > 0) AND boldness falls (B_meta < B_nometa) under metanorms

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce Axelrod's COMPARATIVE result — metanorms raise enforcement (vengefulness) and suppress boldness vs the plain norm — and would catch an artifact. The locked claims are comparative, not 'the norm always establishes'.

citations: Axelrod, R. (1986). An Evolutionary Approach to Norms. American Political Science Review 80(4):1095-1111. doi:10.2307/1960858.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the population-mean vengefulness and boldness, comparing the metanorm vs no-metanorm arm
